subject: Re: Deployment & Data Handling — EU residency, 14d logs, and training exclusion
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Thomas Berg <thomas.berg@clearhealth.eu>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-18T14:17:00Z
Subject: Deployment & Data Handling — EU residency, 14d logs, and training exclusion

Hi Thomas — thanks again for a constructive call earlier. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can lock the configuration for the pilot:  

- ClearHealth requirement summary (as I understood it): EU-only data residency (primary West/EU region), all event logs retained no longer than 14 days, PII fields masked or tokenized before storage, and no use of transaction/telemetry data for model training or improvement (explicit opt-out).
- Action items for Redwood: provide a DPA addendum + SOC2 evidence, confirm technical controls for PII sanitization in the ingestion pipeline, and set a serving flag to prevent training-on-customer-data.

Can you confirm the three bullets above are correct, and whether your legal team prefers a short DPA addendum or an updated master DPA? If you can confirm, we’ll: 1) attach the proposed DPA addendum and SOC2 report, 2) create the DocuSign envelope, and 3) change the runtime config to enforce EU-only and training_excluded=true for your tenant.

Thanks — I’ll hold on the DocuSign until you confirm the wording on retention (14 days) and PII handling.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0127
From: Thomas Berg <thomas.berg@clearhealth.eu>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@clearhealth.eu>
Date: 2027-05-18T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Deployment & Data Handling — EU residency, 14d logs, and training exclusion

Karthik — thanks for the recap. Correct on all three bullets with two small clarifications from our side:  

1) Retention: 14 days for request/response logs and non-PII telemetry. We still need short-term access to aggregated metrics for debugging (also within 14 days) but no long-term storage.
2) PII: We require both automatic PII redaction at ingestion (names, SSNs, device IDs) and a downstream suppression step so any raw user text that is flagged remains inaccessible to model training pipelines.

And yes — ClearHealth prefers a short DPA addendum referencing our existing agreement rather than a full DPA rewrite. Once we see the addendum we’ll route to legal; expect a legal ping if they want editorial tweaks.

Finally, to be explicit: ClearHealth confirms an opt-out of model training on any production traffic. Please treat this as a permanent configuration for the pilot and any subsequent production rollout unless we explicitly notify you otherwise in writing.

Best,
Thomas Berg
Head of Engineering — ClearHealth
thomas.berg@clearhealth.eu | +49 30 1234 5678
